note: Original language puzzles. Stars show how independently a puzzle was solved; they are not a language level or score.

puzzles.title: Walk to School
puzzles.prompt: Tap the words to build a sentence that tells how you get to school.
hints: Start with the word that names who is walking.
A verb comes right after the speaker. Which tile tells what the speaker does?
Two sentences work: you can put "every day" at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: The Sleeping Dog
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about where the dog is.
hints: The word "the" appears twice. One starts the sentence.
Say who it is about first, then "is sleeping".
A place phrase comes last: under + the + table.

puzzles.title: Lunch Question
puzzles.prompt: Build a question that asks about lunch.
hints: Questions with "where" often start with the question word.
After the question word comes a helper word: do.
Then the speaker, the action, and the thing: you eat lunch.

puzzles.title: Stay Inside
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that gives a reason. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: The word "because" starts the reason part.
The reason part is: it was raining. The result part is: we stayed inside.
Put the result first or the reason first. Both are correct.

puzzles.title: Spring Garden
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about planting. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: Find the people: my brother and I.
Then the action and the thing: plant tomatoes.
"In spring" tells when. It can go at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: Although the Test
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that shows a contrast. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Although" begins the part that is surprising.
The "although" part is: the test was difficult. The main part is: most students finished early.
You can put the "although" part first or last.

puzzles.title: Volcano Scientists
puzzles.prompt: Build one sentence that tells which scientists wear special helmets.
hints: The word "who" connects a group of people to a description of them.
The group is "scientists". The description is "who study volcanoes".
After the description comes the main action: wear special helmets.

puzzles.title: Ancient Builders
puzzles.prompt: Build a question about how ancient builders worked.
hints: Start with the question word that asks about the way something was done.
After the question word comes a helper in the past: did. Then the subject.
"Such heavy stones" ends the question. Which describing word comes before "stones"?

puzzles.title: Who Has Which Pet?
puzzles.prompt: Match each friend to a pet. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: pet

clues.text: Ana's pet lives in a bowl of water.
Ben's pet is not the cat.

hints: Start with the clue that tells you exactly one match.
Ana's pet lives in water, so it is the fish. Cross the fish off for Ben and Cy.
Ben's pet is not the cat, and the fish is taken. What is left for Ben?

puzzles.title: Lunch Drinks
puzzles.prompt: Match each student to a drink. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: drink

clues.text: Mia does not drink milk or juice.
Leo drinks either milk or water.

hints: "Does not drink milk or juice" means Mia drinks neither one.
If Mia drinks neither milk nor juice, only one drink is left for her.
Mia has the water. Leo drinks either milk or water, so which one can he have?

puzzles.title: Music Club
puzzles.prompt: Match each student to an instrument. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: instrument

clues.text: Sam does not play the piano.
Sam does not play the violin.
Rita plays either the violin or the drums.

hints: Start with the two clues about Sam. They leave only one instrument.
Sam does not play the piano or the violin, so Sam plays the drums.
Rita plays either the violin or the drums. The drums are taken, so which does she play, and what is left for Tom?

puzzles.title: After-School Activities
puzzles.prompt: Match four friends to four activities. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: activity

clues.text: Ava does not do soccer or chess.
Cara does not do art, band, or chess.
Dev does not do band.
Ava does not do band.

hints: Look for the clue that rules out three activities for one person.
Cara does not do art, band, or chess, so Cara does soccer. Nobody else can do soccer.
Ava does not do soccer, chess, or band, so she does art. Dev cannot do band, so what can Dev do? Then Ben gets the last one.

puzzles.title: Favorite Subjects
puzzles.prompt: Match four students to their favorite subjects. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: favorite subject

clues.text: Neither Elena nor Farid likes math best.
Grace likes either science or history best.
Farid does not like art best.
Grace does not like history best.

hints: Ask: who is allowed to like math best? Check each clue about math.
Elena and Farid cannot, and Grace likes science or history. So Hiro likes math.
With math taken, who can like art? Then use the last clue to decide Grace and Farid.

puzzles.title: Which Word Does Not Belong?
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Cat, dog, and rabbit are animals. A table is furniture.
hints: Say each word aloud. Is there a group of three?
Three of these words name living things.
Which word does not name a living thing?

puzzles.title: Action or Feeling?
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Run, jump, and swim are actions you can do with your body. Happy describes a feeling.
hints: Think about what each word tells you.
Three of these words are things you can do with your body.
Which word tells how someone feels instead of what they do?

puzzles.title: On the Calendar
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Monday, Friday, and Sunday are days of the week. July is a month.
hints: All four words are about time.
Three of them name a short part of a week.
Which word names a longer part of the year?

puzzles.title: Words About the Past
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Ancient, old, and historic describe things from the past. Modern describes the present or recent time.
hints: Think about the time each word points to.
Three words point back to a time long ago.
Which word points to now instead of long ago?

puzzles.title: Connecting Words
puzzles.prompt: Three connecting words do the same job. Find the one that does a different job.
puzzles.rule: In these sentences, because, since, and as give a reason. Although shows a contrast.
hints: Make a short sentence with each word. What job does it do?
Three of the words answer the question "why?".
Which word shows two ideas that seem to go against each other?

puzzles.title: Words for Persuading
puzzles.prompt: Three words have similar meanings. Find the one with a different meaning.
puzzles.rule: Persuade, convince, and urge are about trying to change what someone thinks or does. Ignore means to pay no attention.
hints: Think about what a speaker is doing with each word.
Three words are about talking to someone to change their mind.
Which word means paying no attention at all?

puzzles.title: Recess Game
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about what you do at recess. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: Find the word that names who is playing.
Right after the speaker comes the action, then the thing they play with.
"At recess" tells when. It can go at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: The Biggest Planet
puzzles.prompt: Build a question about the planets.
hints: This is a question. Which tile is a question word?
After the question word comes the verb: is.
"The" comes before the describing word, and the describing word comes before the thing it describes.

puzzles.title: Sleepy Hamster
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about a hamster. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: Find the two words that name the pet: whose pet, then what pet.
Which tile tells what the pet does?
"All day" tells how long. It can go at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: Sports Day
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about sports day. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Ran" is a past tense verb. Who ran? Find the two words that name the group.
After "ran" comes what they ran: a + relay + race.
"Yesterday" tells when. It can go at the start or at the end.

puzzles.title: Too Hot to Eat
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that tells a cause and then a result. Start with the cause.
hints: The word "so" starts the result part of the sentence.
The cause part tells what was wrong with the food: the soup + was + too + hot.
After "so" comes the result: who did something, and what they did.

puzzles.title: Falling Leaves
puzzles.prompt: Build a question about leaves. Two different questions are correct.
hints: Find the question word that asks for a reason.
After the question word comes the helper "do", then the thing, then the action.
"In autumn" tells when. It can go at the end or at the very start.

puzzles.title: Field Trip Day
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence about a class trip. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Visited" is the past tense verb. Who visited? Find the two words that name the group.
What did they visit? The words a + describing word + place go together.
"Last week" tells when. It can go at the start or at the end.

puzzles.title: Arctic Animals
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that gives a reason. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: The word "because" starts the reason part.
The reason part tells about the place: the + Arctic + is + a describing word. The other part tells what the animals have.
Put the reason first or last. Both are correct.

puzzles.title: Recess Games
puzzles.prompt: Match each friend to a recess game. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: game

clues.text: Lina plays jump rope.
Kofi does not play tag.

hints: Start with the clue that tells you one match for sure.
Jump rope belongs to one friend, so nobody else can have it.
Kofi does not play tag. Which game is still open for Kofi? Then who is left?

puzzles.title: Planet Reports
puzzles.prompt: Match each student to the planet in their report. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: planet

clues.text: Omar's report is about the red planet, Mars.
Nora is not writing about Saturn.

hints: One clue names a planet for one student. Start there.
Mars is taken now. Cross it off for Nora and Priya.
Nora is not writing about Saturn. Which planet does that leave for her?

puzzles.title: Cooking Club
puzzles.prompt: Match each cook to a dish. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: dish

clues.text: Neither Sofia nor Tariq makes tacos.
Sofia makes either tacos or soup.

hints: "Neither Sofia nor Tariq" means both of them do not make that dish.
If Sofia and Tariq do not make tacos, only one cook can make them.
Sofia makes either tacos or soup. Tacos are taken, so what does Sofia make? Who gets the last dish?

puzzles.title: Field Trip Vote
puzzles.prompt: Match four friends to the field trip each one wants. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: field trip

clues.text: Hana wants to go to the museum.
Luis does not want to go to the farm or the aquarium.
Jun does not want to go to the farm.

hints: Begin with the clue that names a trip for one friend.
The museum is taken. Luis does not want the farm or the aquarium, so only one trip is left for Luis.
Now two trips are left for Aiyana and Jun. Use the clue about Jun to decide.

puzzles.title: Habitat Posters
puzzles.prompt: Match four students to the habitat on their poster. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: habitat

clues.text: Neither Dara nor Yusuf drew the desert.
Inés drew either the pond or the desert.
Emeka did not draw the pond or the ocean.
Yusuf did not draw the ocean or the pond.

hints: Start with Yusuf. Cross off every habitat a clue says he did not draw.
Yusuf has only one habitat left. Now look at Emeka: which habitats can he still have?
Who is left to draw the desert? Then use the clue about Inés, and give Dara the last one.

puzzles.title: Where Animals Live
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Desert, ocean, and forest are natural habitats where wild animals live. A kitchen is a room in a home.
hints: Picture each place. Who lives there?
Three of these places are part of nature.
Which place is inside a building that people made?

puzzles.title: In the Kitchen
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Stir, mix, and bake are actions you do when you cook. A spoon is a thing you cook with.
hints: Try putting "I" in front of each word: I ___.
Three words are things a cook does.
Which word names a tool you can hold in your hand?

puzzles.title: Weather Words
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Sunny, cloudy, and stormy describe the weather. Sleepy describes how a person feels.
hints: All four words end with -y. Look at what each one describes.
Three words tell what the sky looks like today.
Which word tells how you might feel at bedtime?

puzzles.title: Question Starters
puzzles.prompt: Three words can start a question. Find the one that does a different job.
puzzles.rule: Who, where, and when start questions. Because starts a reason, which is part of an answer.
hints: Try to start a question with each word.
Three words ask about a person, a place, or a time.
Which word do you use to answer the question "Why?"

puzzles.title: Story Order Words
puzzles.prompt: Three words belong together. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: First, next, and then tell the order things happen. Under tells where something is.
hints: Think about telling the steps of a story.
Three words help you tell what happened in order.
Which word tells a position, like where a ball is?

puzzles.title: Yesterday Words
puzzles.prompt: Three words tell about the past. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Ran, swam, and ate tell about the past. They are past tense verbs that do not end in -ed. Sing tells about now.
hints: Put "Yesterday I" in front of each word. Which ones sound right?
Three of the words already show the past, even without -ed.
Which word would need to change to tell about yesterday?

puzzles.title: Describing Words
puzzles.prompt: Three words describe a thing. Find the word that describes an action.
puzzles.rule: Fluffy, gigantic, and shiny are adjectives: they describe nouns, like a fluffy cat. Quickly is an adverb: it describes how someone does an action.
hints: Try each word in front of a noun: a ___ cat.
Three words fit before a noun and tell what it is like.
Which word ends in -ly and tells how someone moves?

puzzles.title: Plants Make Food
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that tells how plants make food. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: Start with the living things the sentence is about.
Next comes what they use. Which tile names a kind of energy?
"To" + a verb tells the purpose. The purpose can go at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: Why Pyramids?
puzzles.prompt: Build a question about ancient Egypt.
hints: Start with the question word that asks for a reason.
A past tense question uses the helper "did". The subject comes right after it.
The base verb and the thing that was built end the question.

puzzles.title: Rolling to a Stop
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that explains a cause. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Because of" is followed by a noun that names the cause.
The cause is a force: because of + friction. The main part tells what the object did.
The cause phrase can go at the end or at the start.

puzzles.title: Unless We Practice
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that warns what will happen if the team does not practice. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Unless" means "if not". It starts the condition part.
The condition part is short: unless + who + the action. The main part tells the result with "will".
The "unless" part can go first or last.

puzzles.title: When the River Dried Up
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that explains why the farmers moved their herds. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: Here "since" means "because". It starts the cause part.
The cause is about water: the + river + dried + up. The result tells what the farmers did.
Put the "since" part first or last, but keep the cause and the result true to the prompt.

puzzles.title: Survey Results
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that reports what a survey found. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "According to" names the source of the information.
The source phrase is: according to + the + survey. The claim tells what most students prefer.
The source phrase can go at the start or at the end of the claim.

puzzles.title: Maya Sky Watchers
puzzles.prompt: Build one sentence about a Maya calendar.
hints: The subject is two words: which people, and what job they had.
After the main verb comes what they made: a + calendar.
"That" begins a description of the calendar. What did it track?

puzzles.title: A King of Mali
puzzles.prompt: Build one sentence about a king of Mali. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Who" connects the king to a description of him.
The sentence has two actions: one goes in the "who" part, and one is the main verb.
Either action can go in the "who" part. Both sentences are true about this king.

puzzles.title: The Students' Plan
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that says the students wrote a plan and the council said yes to it.
hints: Who said yes? That group is the subject: the + council.
The main verb means "said yes to". What did they say yes to?
"That" begins a description of the plan. Who proposed it?

puzzles.title: Farming by the Nile
puzzles.prompt: Build a sentence that shows a contrast. Two different sentences are correct.
hints: "Although" begins the part that makes the main idea surprising.
The "although" part describes the land: their + land + was + a describing word. The main part tells what people did and where.
The "although" part can go first or last.

puzzles.title: Food Web Roles
puzzles.prompt: Match each student to the food web role they are studying. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: role

clues.text: Amara studies the organism that breaks down dead matter: the decomposer.
Ravi is not studying the producer.

hints: One clue gives a definition and names a role for one student.
The decomposer is taken. Cross it off for Ravi and Lucía.
Ravi is not studying the producer. Which role does that leave for him?

puzzles.title: Forces Lab
puzzles.prompt: Match each student to a lab station. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: station

clues.text: Neither Bilal nor Chen is at the friction station.
Chen is at either the gravity station or the friction station.

hints: "Neither ... nor" rules out one station for two students at once.
Only one student can be at the friction station.
Chen is at one of two stations, and one of them is now taken.

puzzles.title: Ancient Civilizations
puzzles.prompt: Match four students to the civilization each one researched. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: civilization

clues.text: Neither Kwame nor Zara researched the Maya.
Tenzin researched either Han China or Egypt.
Zara did not research Mali or Han China.

hints: Find the student with the most civilizations ruled out. Check every clue that names her.
Zara is left with only one civilization. That decides Tenzin's clue too.
Two civilizations are left for Kwame and Marisol. Which one can Kwame not have?

puzzles.title: Graph Makers
puzzles.prompt: Match four students to the graph each one made for a data project. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: graph

clues.text: Neither Nadia nor Quynh made the bar graph.
Quynh did not make the line graph.
Olu made either the dot plot or the bar graph.
Olu did not make the bar graph.

hints: Two clues are about Olu. Use them together first.
Now ask: who is still allowed to make the bar graph?
Two graphs are left for Nadia and Quynh. One clue rules out a graph for Quynh.

puzzles.title: Student Council
puzzles.prompt: Match four students to their student council jobs. Use every clue.
puzzles.label: job

clues.text: Neither Rosa nor Uma is the president.
Samir is not the president or the treasurer.
Rosa is either the treasurer or the reporter.
Samir is not the secretary.

hints: Ask: who is allowed to be the president? Check every clue that mentions that job.
Now look at Samir. After you cross off three jobs, how many are left?
With Samir's job decided, Rosa's clue leaves her one choice. Uma gets the job that is left.

puzzles.title: Food Web Groups
puzzles.prompt: Three living things belong to the same food web group. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Grass, algae, and an oak tree are producers: they make their own food from sunlight. A rabbit is a consumer: it eats other living things.
hints: Ask how each living thing gets its energy.
Three of them use sunlight to make their own food.
Which one has to eat plants to get energy?

puzzles.title: Ancient Egypt
puzzles.prompt: Three words name people in ancient Egypt. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Pharaoh, scribe, and priest are roles people had in ancient Egypt. Papyrus is a plant material that Egyptians wrote on.
hints: Ask of each word: is this a person or a thing?
Three words name jobs or roles in Egyptian society.
Which word names a material that a writer used, not the writer?

puzzles.title: Contrast Connectors
puzzles.prompt: Three connecting words do the same job. Find the one that does a different job.
puzzles.rule: However, but, and although show a contrast between two ideas. Therefore shows a result or conclusion.
hints: Write two short sentences and join them with each word. What does the word signal?
Three words signal that the next idea goes against the first one.
Which word signals that the next idea follows from the first one?

puzzles.title: Forces in Science
puzzles.prompt: Three words name forces. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Gravity, friction, and magnetism are forces: pushes or pulls on an object. Mass is the amount of matter in an object, not a force.
hints: A force is a push or a pull. Test each word against that definition.
Three words can make an object speed up, slow down, or change direction.
Which word measures how much matter an object has?

puzzles.title: Checking a Claim
puzzles.prompt: Three words name things you can check to support a claim. Find the one that does not.
puzzles.rule: Evidence, data, and results are facts or measurements other people can check. An opinion is what someone believes or feels, so it cannot be proven true or false.
hints: Ask of each word: could another person check this and get the same answer?
Three words come from facts, tests, or measurements.
Which word names a personal belief?

puzzles.title: Verbs of Argument
puzzles.prompt: Three verbs show a writer taking a position. Find the verb that does not.
puzzles.rule: Claim, argue, and assert all mean stating a position and defending it. Describe means telling what something is like, without taking a side.
hints: Put each verb in this frame: The author ___ that ...
Three verbs tell you the author is taking a side.
Which verb tells you the author is reporting details instead of taking a side?

puzzles.title: The Root Port
puzzles.prompt: Three words share the Latin root port, meaning "carry". Find the word that only looks like it does.
puzzles.rule: Transport (carry across), portable (able to be carried), and export (carry out of a country) all use the root port, meaning carry. Portrait comes from the word portray, meaning to draw or show. It has nothing to do with carrying.
hints: For each word, ask: is something being carried?
Three words describe moving or carrying goods or objects.
Which word names a picture of a person?
